meta.move: Strong path: owns the missed call, then evidence in order, then the rewrite
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have twenty minutes before a client call, so let's use them. Who decided to put a zero on Owen's essay, and why did I find out from my son's phone?
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for coming in. Before anything else: I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. That's one thing. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went in?

Here's what I can show you. The document's version history: created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, title only. At 11:52, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, another 794. No drafts before that.
I'm writing down your times. Procedure 4.1 says you speak with the student first, and you still haven't told me you did. I'll want that history printed and sent to me in an email.
Second, the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the scene; you can search it yourself.
I'm searching the scene now. Students misquote plays every year, and a wrong line is a wrong line. What makes it more than that?

Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. We could do it in my room, Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising.

That's 4.4. I want it in writing: the zero off the gradebook today, nothing placed on his record, and no one in his class told. You still haven't answered me about the line, Hale, so I'm not agreeing to Thursday yet.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero removed from the gradebook, nothing placed on Owen's record, and no one in his class told, all confirmed in writing. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her fallback position, since your offer met her demand about his record but she did not accept the rewrite, and she still wants the zero off the gradebook, nothing on file, and everything in writing; that is close to the fair outcome (a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record, procedure 4.4), but it was not settled, and her time had not run out.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling her and then offered the supervised rewrite under the first-concern procedure, which gave her the protection for his record that she most needed.
What cost ground: You offered the rewrite before answering her question about the wrong line, which left her objection standing and let her refuse to commit.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with its late-night times the night before it was due, came very close to that night, but it proves nothing about the essay, and it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked what made the line more than a misquote, answer her with the late-night edit times and the wrong line together, and only then offer the rewrite.
